annotationRationale: Parity bounds how many even entries one move can remove. An explicit sequence attains the resulting upper bound on the final number of entries.
sourceMethod: Followed the official bound of three even entries removed per operation and its construction using blocks of six. Explained why the chosen original entries remain available and why every replacement sum is odd.

review.mathCheck: Each move decreases the even-entry count by at most 3, so eliminating 1012 evens requires at least 338 moves, leaving at most 1010 entries. The 337 disjoint blocks produce odd sums 24n+13 and remove exactly the evens through 2022. The unused entries 3,5,9,2024 produce the final odd sum 2041. Thus 1010 is attainable, confirming A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 16, page 8: the same even-removal bound and attaining construction. The candidate additionally explains the parity bound and verifies that all selected original entries remain available.
review.annotationCheck: Both direct nodes are relevant. The extremal node captures the universal bound and construction; cnm_p156 supplies the elementary parity component. No material annotation omission.
